The Morph Labs team is excited to announce the public beta for Moogle, a semantic search engine for mathlib.

Moogle lets you use natural language to find theorems from mathlib faster. It builds on some of the same techniques as our recent Morph Prover v0 7B model.

We will improve Moogle based on your feedback. If a search result doesn’t match your expectations, please let us know using the thumbs-up/down buttons in the UI.

moogle-GIF.gif
4 messages were moved from this topic to #general > Moogle discussion by Kyle Miller.

Moogle v2 is live! https://moogle.ai

  • 99% coverage of all declarations including all instances in mathlib
  • even with more than 50K new declarations in the search index, we improved our semantic search engine so that it retrieves even more relevant results than before (better top-1 recall on the same test set)
  • docgen4-like links to terms in search results

Over 1,200 users have issued >6,000 searches in the past week, and Terry Tao mentioned using Moogle for finding key lemmas for his Maclaurin-type inequality formalization.

moogle-v2-final.gif

Announcing Moogle v3! https://moogle.ai

The Morph team is excited to release the next iteration of Moogle.

moogle-v3-final.gif

  • Moogle now supports Loogle-like #find syntax for hybrid searches. Type #find in the search bar to create a pattern-matching query, and combine it with natural language to get the most relevant results. Please note that our backend for #find forks Loogle and may return different results.
  • Moogle is now available in a VSCode extension. It is very simple at the moment and will quickly improve.

Happy formalizing!
